title: Set multicover with repeated sets

problem.name: Set multicover with repeated sets
problem.statement_latex:
Given $\mathcal F=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}\subseteq2^{[n]}$ and a fixed demand $D\geq1$, minimize $\sum_jx_j$ over integers $x_j\geq0$ satisfying $\sum_{j:i\in S_j}x_j\geq D$ for every $i$. Here a set may be selected repeatedly. This models redundant coverage or repeated resource provision.
The quantum algorithm is measured in QRAM time, classical lattice dynamic programming in RAM time, and the bounded-incidence encoding in bit operations.
problem.statement_text: Given $\mathcal F=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}\subseteq2^{[n]}$ and a fixed demand $D\geq1$, minimize $\sum_jx_j$ over integers $x_j\geq0$ satisfying $\sum_{j:i\in S_j}x_j\geq D$ for every $i$. Here a set may be selected repeatedly. This models redundant coverage or repeated resource provision. The quantum algorithm is measured in QRAM time, classical lattice dynamic programming in RAM time, and the bounded-incidence encoding in bit operations.

quantum.details_latex: For fixed $D$, the base satisfies $T_D<D+1$, with $T_2<2.660$, $T_3<3.529$ and $T_4<4.421$. The quasipolynomial prefactor is part of the bound. Coherent access to precomputed lattice states is assumed. Truncating coverage coordinates at $D$ retains all relevant states, and no set needs multiplicity above $D$.
quantum.details_text: For fixed $D$, the base satisfies $T_D<D+1$, with $T_2<2.660$, $T_3<3.529$ and $T_4<4.421$. The quasipolynomial prefactor is part of the bound. classical.details_latex: The state space consists of capped coverage vectors in $\{0,\ldots,D\}^n$. Let $I=\sum_j|S_j|$ be the incidence count. When $m+I=O(n)$ and $D$ is fixed, a linear-size bounded-width Boolean encoding gives the stronger deterministic bound $\operatorname{poly}(m,n)2^{O_D(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ with polynomial space. This includes the multiplicity variables, capped local coverage sums and objective threshold.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for fixed demand in the general lattice comparison, using quantum search. Linear-incidence instances have a subexponential classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous QRAM upper bound and partial evidence against the best general classical lattice algorithm.

hardware.description_latex:
The active coverage register has $O(n\log(D+1))$ qubits, with polynomial workspace and exponential coherent preprocessing storage. The dependence on $D$ affects both the lattice size and reversible arithmetic.
{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the lattice comparison used $O(m(D+1)^n)$ classically and $\operatorname{poly}(m,n)^{\log n}T_D^n$ quantumly, including the linear-incidence regime now covered by the subexponential bound.]\par}
